title: Prove a module's runtime is alive: the runtime demo ping, read-only, with the refusals
description: The ping is a read and changes nothing. A company administrator calls GET /api/v1/modules/runtime_demo/ping: 200 {runtime_demo: true, release} when the module is installed in that company, 404 when it is not; the file says which half ran (step s2 is skipped with 'requires demo_release' on 404). A storekeeper is refused (403, or 404 when the module is not installed) and a caller without a sign-in gets 401. NOT automated, and a GAP rather than an invented behaviour: the install of the module (POST /api/v1/tenant/modules), the three releases (0.1.0, 0.2.0, 0.3.0 are a boot setting LETFLOW_RUNTIME_DEMO_RELEASE of the host, changed by recreating the container) and the 503 answers module_version_ahead and module_upgrade_required of the version-skew gate need an installed module in a company whose administrator the runner can sign in as, and a host change by the operator (docs/runbooks/runtime-demo-module.md, 'The sequence'); they are covered by test/letflow/modules/runtime_demo/router_test.exs. Nothing is installed or changed by this file, so there is no cleanup and no residue; the fixture tenant is not needed.

steps.says: A company administrator calls the demo module's ping. 200 when the module is installed in the company; 404 when it is not (the module exists only in a QA build made with the demo flag, and nothing installs it for a company). The release is remembered only when the module answers.
INSTALLED: the ping answers runtime_demo true and the release it remembered.
A storekeeper does not hold the permission (it is granted to the company administrator only): refused with 403, or 404 when the module is not installed.
Without a sign-in the ping is refused: 401.
